subject: Dev kit ramp: SDK environment & routing checklist for Drift Analytics
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Torres <sam@drift-analytics.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer, neha_kapoor
Date: 2026-10-12T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Dev kit ramp: SDK environment & routing checklist for Drift Analytics

Hi Sam — great chat earlier, thanks for the context. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we can get your engineers up and running with a local SDK sandbox.

Summary of scope we discussed:
- Primary objective: prototype semantic search + reranker on support tickets (embeddings -> ANN index + rerank on top-k).
- Target environments: you noted preference for private deployment (VPC) and KMS-backed keys for production, but want a local/dev path to validate integration.
- Routing: multi-region read-traffic (us-east primary, fallback to us-west) and a low-latency path for synchronous agent flows.
- Structured output/tool-calling: define a schema for action items and instrument tool hooks for ticket triage.

Immediate asks / blockers for your team:
1) Confirm the technical contact who will install/run the samples (you mentioned Priya; can you confirm email?).
2) Confirm whether you can run Docker locally (we provide a containerized example) or prefer raw Python/Node installs.
3) Any strict egress/KMS constraints we should validate in the sample.

Local quickstart (recommended first steps) - attach: redwood-sdk-python-sample.zip and integration-matrix.xlsx
- Clone repo: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/drift-samples.git
- Python (venv recommended):
  python3 -m venv venv
  source venv/bin/activate
  pip install -r requirements.txt
- Set env vars:
  export REDWOOD_API_KEY=your_test_key_here
  export REDWOOD_REGION=us-east-1
- Run sample server:
  python samples/semantic_server.py --model redwood-l2 --port 8080
- Node/TS quick test (optional):
  cd samples/ts
  npm install
  REDWOOD_API_KEY=your_test_key node dist/run_sample.js

Notes on model variants for local testing:
- Use a quantized small variant (redwood-l2-quant) for single-GPU local dev to keep memory modest.
- For production, we recommend the full redwood-l2 family in your Dedicated pool.

Routing & auth guidance:
- Auth: for dev, API keys are fine. For VPC/private, we recommend short-lived tokens sourced from your KMS/HSM via our private control plane.
- Routing: we'll provide a sample policy yaml to route by region + fallback; it lives in the repo under infra/routing_examples.yml.

Next steps I propose:
- Priya (technical) and your infra engineer try the Python sample and report back any install errors by EOD Friday.
- We (Karthik + Neha) will prepare the routing yaml and a sample structured output schema for the tool-calling flow.
- 30-minute follow-up on Tue 10/15 to validate the local run and review embedding index sizing.

Thanks — attaching a short onramp guide and the integration matrix for you to fill (mapping of data sources, PII constraints, throughput targets).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
Phone: (415) 555-0192

Attachments:
- redwood-sdk-python-sample.zip (python samples + dockerfile)
- integration-matrix.xlsx (table: data sources, retention, throughput targets)
- redwood-onramp-guide.pdf (high level steps)

Internal notes + concrete runbook to drop in the repo. Posting here so Priya/Sam see the commands too.

1) If Priya sees "CUDA out of memory" on 32GB boxes, switch to the quantized variant and reduce batch_size to 1:
  export MODEL=redwood-l2-quant
  python samples/semantic_server.py --model $MODEL --batch_size 1 --port 8080

2) Docker quickstart (recommended to avoid local dependency drift):
  docker build -t redwood-sample:latest -f samples/Dockerfile .
  docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 -e REDWOOD_API_KEY="$REDWOOD_API_KEY" redwood-sample:latest

3) Node/TS snippet (samples/ts/run_sample.js):
  const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/inference');
  const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
  const resp = await client.embeddings.create({ model: 'redwood-embed-l1', input: 'support ticket text' });

4) Routing policy (example):
  - primary: us-east (latency optimized)
  - fallback: us-west (cost fallback)
  - canary: small % to dedicated pool for stress testing

5) Structured output / tool calling: use JSON schema (samples/schema/triage_action.json) — server returns a wrapper: {"actions": [...], "tools": [...] } and we validate server-side before executing tool calls.

I'll push integration-matrix.xlsx with our suggested throughput targets and a draft routing yaml to the repo by EOD. Adding a HubSpot task: HS-39821 to track the pilot scripts.

-karthik
